patches.OLD_TEXT: the visitor arrives at a name that was not in their possession an hour earlier
patches.NEW_TEXT: the visitor arrives at a name they have never heard of
patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: You can't walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you've never heard of.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source supports only the visitor's unfamiliarity with the names encountered. It establishes no timeline, so the invented interval 'an hour earlier' is removed and only the source-supported unfamiliarity is kept.

patches.OLD_TEXT: And that second obligation is harder to discharge, because the subject is not in the room to say whether it has been met.
patches.NEW_TEXT: Read one way, that second obligation is the harder of the two to discharge, since the subject is not in the room to say whether it has been met.
patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: If contemporary artists and institutions want to tell hidden stories, I think they have a duty - to viewers and to their subjects - to tell them clearly.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source names the two directions of the duty but says nothing about their relative difficulty and does not generalise that subjects are absent. The comparative and its causal explanation are marked as the article's own reading rather than settled fact.

patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: By the time you're done with Edinburgh art festival you'll have uncovered so many hidden stories you'll feel like Columbo.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source never states when the festival takes place; 'in August' is imported from outside knowledge. The month is deleted, leaving the source-supported location.
